text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — support got a customer (TKT-8421) complaining about p95 latency jumps starting ~09:10 PST. They attached traces that show tails, but our grafana p95 panel doesn’t move. Can someone sanity-check?

Jon Patel: I saw an alert from synthetic monitors around the same time, but our infra metrics p95 stayed flat. Could be a label mismatch on the dashboard query.

Keiko Tanaka: Which dashboard panel? the /v1/generate per-route panel or the global api.p95 recording rule? Those use different aggregation labels.

Maria Chen: The customer called out /v1/generate with model:redwood-large. Panel they pointed at is /dashboards/latency -> "API p95" (looks global).

Carlos Lopez (support): Adding customer notes — they see intermittent 300-800ms spikes at p95, p99 up to 1.6s. Spikes align with high concurrency from their side, not huge traffic overall. They provided a request ID: req_0a3f9e.

Samir Ahmed: Possible causes: (1) snapshot mis-specified as a histogram vs summary, (2) dashboard using histogram_quantile on bucketed metrics with different bucket boundaries, (3) sample-window mismatch between PromQL and how we compute p95 for billing/alerts.

Keiko Tanaka: I pulled the panel query — it’s `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))` but it's missing `by (route, model)` in the inner sum. That aggregates across all routes/models, then calculates quantile which can hide per-route tails.

Maria Chen: So a per-route spike could be flattened in the global quantile? I thought quantiles over aggregated histograms are approximate, but this sounds like it could mask spikes.

Jon Patel: Exactly. histogram_quantile on an aggregate of histograms is not the same as aggregating quantiles. If one route has a heavy tail and others are low, the aggregated histogram might give a different 95th. Also bucket alignment matters — if some exporters used different le boundaries, you'd get inconsistent buckets.

Keiko Tanaka: I checked Prometheus scrape targets: runtime exporters (inference runtime) and proxy exporter both expose buckets. Found a small mismatch: runtime buckets are canonical: [0.005,0.01,0.025,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,1,2.5,5] while an old sidecar uses [0.01,0.02,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,1,2.5,5]. The missing 0.005/0.025 vs 0.02 means histogram_quantile could be off at low tails.

observability-bot: automated note — related alert rule `HighTailLatency` fired 1742004568 for route="/v1/generate" model="redwood-large" in us-west-2. Recording rule `redwood_api_p95` has last evaluation 1742004565.

Samir Ahmed: That sidecar is scheduled to be rotated in staging but somehow one ded pool had the old version in prod. Might explain bucket mismatch. Good catch Keiko.

Maria Chen: For immediate debugging, can someone run these queries and paste the raw histogram bucket outputs for route=/v1/generate and model=redwood-large?

Jon Patel: Running now:
```
sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",model="redwood-large"}[5m])) by (le)
```
Output snippet: `le="0.01": 124.2, le="0.025": 129.9, le="0.05": 130.0, le="0.1": 130.0, le="0.25": 130.0, le="0.5": 130.0, le="1": 130.0, le="2.5": 130.0, le="5": 130.0`

Keiko Tanaka: Sidecar output (older bucket set) for same selector: `le="0.01": 210.3, le="0.02": 211.0, le="0.05": 211.1, le="0.1": 211.1 ...` — totals differ because one target reports finer-binned counts at 5ms and 20ms which changes the quantile interpolation.

Maria Chen: So dashboard p95 might under-report global p95 for that route. But the customer sees high p95 — this suggests the customer's observed p95 is correct, Prometheus panel is wrong (or at least misleading).

Samir Ahmed: Short-term mitigation: create a route-scoped panel and alert that computes histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le,route,model)(rate(...))). For the alerting rule, use recording rules to pre-aggregate by route+model to ensure consistent calculations.

Keiko Tanaka: Long-term: we need uniform histogram buckets across all exporters. Action item: update sidecar to use canonical bucket list and deploy a rolling restart. Also add a unit test in exporter CI to fail if bucket set diverges.

Jon Patel: Also we should validate that the recording rule `redwood_api_p95` is defined as `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le,route,model)(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))` — currently it's `sum by (le)(...)`. I'll open a PR to fix the rule and add a follow-up to re-evaluate historical alerts.

Carlos Lopez (support): What should I tell the customer? They want ETA.

Maria Chen: Tell them: we found a mismatch in how p95 is computed in our global dashboard vs per-route (internal exporters had inconsistent histogram buckets). We already flagged it; short-term we're adding a route-level alert and a dashboard that will show the true per-route p95. Rolling fixes to sidecars and a recording rule change are planned — ETA 2-3 hours for the alert/dashboard patch and bucket rollout start, 24h for full roll. I'll cc: them after we flip the alert.

Samir Ahmed: Additional suggestion: for tail issues enable temporary per-request tracing for the customer (sample rate 1.0 for their org) so we can capture RVs and exact latencies to cross-check. Need approval from security but fine for short-term debugging.

Keiko Tanaka: I'm going to: (1) deploy sidecar bucket fix to canary pool, (2) update exporter CI, (3) change recording rule and push PR. Will post PR/links.

Jon Patel: I'm changing the grafana panel to route-scoped and will add a tooltip explaining bucket/aggregation caveats. Also updating the alert threshold to use the route-level p95.

Maria Chen: Cool. Samir, please enable per-org tracing once we have support opt-in. Carlos, please tell customer we have a fix in progress and we'll share the route-level graph in ~30m.

observability-bot: reminder — make sure to bump the alert suppression window while we deploy to avoid noisy firing.

Samir Ahmed: Noted. I'll silence the noisy global alert for 1 hour and enable the new route-level alert.

Keiko Tanaka: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/PR-4987 — includes sidecar bucket change + CI test. Rolling to canary now.

Jon Patel: Dashboard patch -> https://grafana.redwood/d/abcd1234/latency?orgId=1 (updated panels).

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: Keiko -> confirm canary buckets, Jon -> confirm panel/query & alert, Samir -> tracing + suppression, Carlos -> update customer. We'll reconvene in thread in 45m. :thumbsup:
